Revision 0: April 28, 2017 Place of Publication: India Title: *Urdhvāmnāyapūjāvidhi* (The Ritual Procedure for Worship According to the Upper Tradition)
1. Oṃ, homage to the Illustrious Supreme Deity; homage to the Illustrious Guru.
Homage to the Guru.
Salutation to that glorious Guru, by whom that state has been revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
Then, preceded by the washing of the feet.
"Oṃ, obeisance to the deities of the door. Having thus worshipped, one should enter the house.
Having taken up the unblemished [offering].
Oṃ! May those beings who dwell in heaven, on earth, and in the intermediate space depart from you;
may those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.
With a sharp, keen, and joyful gaze, perform three claps of the hands with a snapping sound (sphoṭa-tāla) three times, and likewise three times with the foot.
Thus ends the dispelling of obstacles. [Direction: Nairṛtya.
Oṃ, homage to Brahmā, the lord of the site. Worship of the seat.
2b) Ai&: Homage to the Tortoise Seat (Kūrmāsana). Having sat upon the seat.
To Gaṇapati, salutation on the right; to the Gurus, salutation on the left.
In front: Oṃ, salutation to the illustrious Mahātripurasundarī.
Having thus prostrated.
Homage to Indra and the other guardians of the world.
Prāṇāyāma according to the sequence of elemental purification (bhūtaśuddhi).

There, with the mantra "so'ham," having united the individual soul (jīvātman) from the heart through the path of the *suṣumnā* with the Supreme Soul (paramātman) residing in the thousand-petaled lotus at the head, and having considered that body— the personification of sin— to have been dried up by the seed-syllable *yaṃ* through the process of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), [he should contemplate it] with the syllable *raṃ*.

Having contemplated [the body] as burnt by the seed-syllable *vaṃ*, having caused a rain of nectar to fall by means of the seed-syllable *laṃ* thirty-two times, and having considered the divine body produced by the nectar of the seed-syllable *vaṃ*, one should [unite] the individual soul (*jīvātman*) with the Supreme Soul (*paramātman*) there by means of the mantra "Haṃsa."
"One should bring [the self] into the heart"—this is the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Then, having placed the mantra "Oṃ Āṃ So'haṃ" upon the heart, one should recite it three times; this is the consecration of the vital breath (prāṇapratiṣṭhā).
Having performed three rounds of breath control (prāṇāyāma) accompanied by the utterance of the syllable Om (praṇava).
Now follows the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

Of this Śrīmātṛkā-mantra: 4a) Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), the Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), the goddess Śrīmātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bīja), the vowels are the powers (śakti), and its application (viniyoga) is in the ritual placement of the letters (lipinyāsa) as a limb of the Śrīvidyā.
Having thus recollected, one should place [the mantra] on the head: *oṃ brahmaṇe ṛṣaye namaḥ*; [and] on the mouth.
Salutation to the Gāyatrī metre. Heart.
Oṃ, homage to the deity Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī.
4b) At the *mūlādhāra*: Oṃ, homage to the seed-syllables beginning with *ha*.
At the two feet: Oṃ, salutation to the vowels and the Śaktis.
One should perform the placement of the hollowed palms; this is the ritual placement of the seers and so forth (ṛṣyādi-nyāsa).
Ṛ& Ṝ& Ḷ& Ḹ& to the weapon, phaṭ 4.
The purification of the hands.
Now follows the ritual placement on the hands.
Oṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ, homage to the heart.
5a) iṃ caṃ 5 īṃ, svāhā to the head. Oṃ ṭaṃ 5 ūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Aiṃ Taṃ 5 Aiṃ, Hūṃ for the armor (kavaca). Oṃ Paṃ 5 Auṃ, Vauṣaṭ for the three eyes (netratraya).
Oṃ aṃ yaṃ [repeated ten times] aḥ astrāya phaṭ.

Thus, having performed the placement (nyāsa) of the six-limbed mantras from the thumb to the tips of the fingers, and having again performed the triple-sound and double-binding with the Astra-mantra, one should perform the placement on the heart and the other six limbs using their respective mudrās; this is the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
5b) Now, the meditation on the Mātṛkā.
Her face, arms, and the region between her shoulders and chest are adorned with the fifty letters of the alphabet;
she wears a radiant crown with a crescent moon; her breasts are full and high;
and she holds in her lotus-like hands the gestures of teaching (*mudrā*), a rosary, a vessel of nectar, and the *vidyā* [script].
I take refuge in the Goddess of Speech, who possesses three eyes and radiant, pure luster.
6a) The internal *mātṛkā*.

In the support [of the body], in the lotuses at the genitals, the navel, the heart, the root of the palate, and the forehead; in those with two petals, sixteen petals, twelve petals, ten petals, ten petals, six petals, four petals;
at the end of the dwelling, in the middle of the hair, together with the fire and the throat, and in the region of the neck, [are placed] the vowels and the syllables *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ*.
I bow to that which is endowed with the true meaning, possessed of sixty-four petals, and whose form is composed of letters.
6b) In the throat there are twelve vowels (svarahṛdika), ten in the navel (nābhiḍa), six in the genitals (liṅgava), and four in the foundation (ādhāra); in the center, however, are ha and kṣa.
Then one should place [the syllables] as follows: on the head, *aṃ* namaḥ; on the mouth, *āṃ* namaḥ; on the right eye, *iṃ* namaḥ.
On the left eye: *īṃ* namaḥ. On the right ear: *oṃ* namaḥ. On the left ear: *ūṃ* namaḥ.
In the right nostril.
7a) Ṛ & Namaḥ. On the left nostril: Jha & Namaḥ. On the right cheek: Ḍha & Namaḥ.
On the left cheek: Ḍhaṃ Namaḥ. On the lip: Aiṃ Namaḥ.
Adhaca aiṃ namaḥ. Ūrdhvadantapaṅktau oṃ namaḥ.
Below: auṃ, obeisance. On the head: aṃ, obeisance. In the mouth: aḥ, obeisance.
At the base of the right arm: *kaṃ* namaḥ. At the middle joint: *khaṃ* namaḥ.
At the wrist: Gaṃ, obeisance.
7b) At the base of the fingers: Ghaṃ Namaḥ. At the tips of the fingers: Ḍhaṃ Namaḥ.
Likewise, on the left as well: cha, ja, jha, ña, namaḥ.
At the root of the right thigh: *ṭaṃ* *namaḥ*. At the knee: *ṭhaṃ* *namaḥ*.
Ḍaṃ, obeisance to the ankle; Ḍhaṃ, obeisance to the base of the toes.
On the tip of the [right] toe: taṃ thaṃ dhaṃ naṃ namaḥ. Likewise on the left foot: taṃ thaṃ dhaṃ naṃ namaḥ.
On the right side: *paṃ* *namaḥ*.
8a) On the left side: *phaṃ* *namaḥ*. On the back: *vaṃ* *namaḥ*.
Salutation to Bhaṃ at the navel. Salutation to Maṃ in the stomach.
Yaṃ at the heart, homage! Yaṃ at the heart, homage!
On the right side, *raṃ*—homage! On the hump, *laṃ*—homage!
On the left shoulder: *vaṃ* *namaḥ*. On the right arm from the heart onwards: *śaṃ* *namaḥ*.
To the left channel from the heart and so forth, ṢAṂ, homage!
At the heart and so forth, up to the right foot: *saṃ* *namaḥ*. At the heart and so forth, up to the left foot: *haṃ* *namaḥ*.
8b) Laṃ, homage to the belly and so forth; kṣaṃ, homage to the mouth and so forth.
Thus one should place [the seed-syllables] without using the nose.
Thus ends the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

Then, one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) with the root-mantra as follows: reciting the root-mantra once while filling the air through the left nostril, one should close both nostrils with the little finger, the ring finger, and the thumb.

9a) While reciting the root mantra four times while retaining [the breath], one should arrest that wind; then, reciting it twice, one should exhale the wind through the right nostril—this is one *prāṇāyāma*.
Again, having filled [the breath] through the right [nostril] in the same manner and retained it, one should exhale through the left nostril; this is another.

In this manner, by way of reversal, one should perform sixteen, twelve, six, three, or three repetitions according to one's capacity, likewise at the end of the recitation and at the beginning of the recitation.
9b) Thus concludes the procedure for breath control (prāṇāyāma).
Now follows the placement (nyāsa) of the Yoga-pīṭha.
Having meditated upon one's own body as the form of the yoga-pīṭha consisting of two arms and four legs, one should place [the seed-syllables] there on the right shoulder.
Oṃ, salutation to Dharma. On the left shoulder, salutation to Jñānāyanā.
Salutation to Vairājñī on the left thigh.
10a) To Dakṣārā, for sovereignty, obeisance! To the mouth, for non-dharma, obeisance!
On the left side: salutation to Ajñāna (Ignorance). On the navel: salutation to Avairājñā (Non-hostile Ignorance).
On the right side: *Namaḥ* to Anaiśvaryā. In the center: to Vāmā, to Vidyā, to Śeṣā;

to the Lotus whose root is Bliss (*ānandakanda*), whose stalk is Consciousness (*savinnāla*), and which is the essence of all principles (*sarvatattvātman*); therein, [homage] to the petals consisting of Prakṛti, to the filaments consisting of the transformations (*vikāra*), and to that which is enriched by the seeds of the fifty letters and is the form of all principles.
Salutation to Karṇikā.

10b) In that [space], [I offer] *aṃ* to the solar disc, *oṃ* to the lunar disc, *maṃ* to the fire disc, *saṃ* to goodness (*sattva*), *raṃ* to passion (*rajas*), and *taṃ* to darkness (*tamas*); homage!
Āṃ, salutation to the Self; Aṃ, to the Inner Self; Paṃ, to the Supreme Self; Hrīṃ, salutation to the Self of Knowledge.

11a) Then: Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O you who are presided over by the hosts of Yoginīs; O you who delude the three worlds; O you who fulfill all desires; O you who cause universal agitation; O you who bestow all good fortune; [you who belong to] the entire tradition—manifest, secret, and most secret—of Kula, Kaula, Nigarbha, and Rahasya; O you who are the supreme, the intermediate-supreme, and the most intensely secret mystery.

Having performed the triple placement (*tripaka-vinyāsa*) with the words: "Obeisance to the sandals of the Śrīcakra, which accomplishes all, which provides all protection, which removes all diseases, which bestows all perfections, and whose nature is the illusion of universal bliss," one should meditate on the body as having the form of the Śrīcakra; and within the center of the heart, [one should meditate on] Bālā in the middle of the triangle.
Having recited the root mantra, [one says] "Oṃ Mahoḍyāna-pīṭhāya namaḥ" in the southeast corner; having recited the two Vāgbhava mantras, [one says] "Kāmarūpa-pīṭhāya namaḥ."
12a) In the left corner: homage to the two Kāmarājas at the Jālandhara-pīṭha.
In the southern corner, the two seed-syllables of Śakti; in the center, for the Pīṭha of Pūrṇagiri: *namaḥ*; [the syllable] *lāṃ* for Agni;
*namaḥ* to Brahmā, the lord of the earth, and *namaḥ* to the Pretāsana.
To the southwest, salutation to Viṣṇu, the lord of waters; salutation to Viṣṇu, whose seat is the corpse.
12b) In the northwest: RĀṂ! Salutation to Rudrāyata, the lord of the *jā* [class]; salutation to Rudra, whose seat is the *preta*.
Aiṃ! For peace; yaṃ! To the Lord, the sovereign of the vital breaths, obeisance; obeisance to the one whose seat is the corpse of the Lord.
In the middle.
Hsauṃ! Salutation to Sadāśiva, the lord of the Vidyādharas and others, who has five faces and whose seat is a great corpse-lotus.
Above that, HRĪM KLĪM SAUḤ, obeisance to the seat of the Self of the Goddess.
HAIṂ HKLĪṂ HSKAUṂ, obeisance to the seat of all cakras.
Hskau& Hsklī& Hskauḥ, homage to the seat of all mantras.
Hrīṃ Klīṃ Vleṃ, salutation to the seat of the one to be accomplished and the perfected ones.
Above that, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sauḥ; salutation to the Form of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī.

Having performed the placement (nyāsa) of the invocation mantra *hsrau& hsklrī& hsrauḥ namaḥ*, and having performed the placement of the root mantra together with its seed-syllables (*savīja*) while reciting "Obeisance to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī," one should contemplate the Supreme Deity upon the seat consisting of the body; this is the placement of the Yoga-seat (*yogapīṭha-nyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the root mantra. Therein, first is the ritual placement of the seer (ṛṣi) and the others.

Having remembered: "The seer (ṛṣi) of this Śrīvidyā is Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the meter (chandas) is Paṅkti, the deity (devatā) is Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the seed-syllable (bīja) is Aiṃ, the power (śakti) is Sauḥ, the peg (kīlaka) is Klīṃ; the application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of all human goals," one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa).
14a) On the head: Oṃ, salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Ṛṣi.
At the mouth: Oṃ, salutation to the Paṅkti metre.
Salutation to the deity Śrī Mahātripurasundarī in the heart.
14b) Having thus performed the placement with the five fingers, [one says] "aiṃ bījāya namaḥ" on the right breast.
On the left breast: *sauḥ* *śaktaye namaḥ*. In the center: *oṃ klīṃ* *kālakāya namaḥ*.
Thus, one should perform the placement with the thumb of the hand free from disease; this is the ritual placement of the seer and so forth.
Now follows the ritual assignment (nyāsa) of the hand-limbs: Aiṃ, salutation to the heart.
Klīṃ, svāhā to the head.
15a) *Sauḥ* to the crest-lock, *vaṣaṭ*; *Aiṃ* to the armor, *hūṃ*.
KLĪM, VAUṢAṬ to the three eyes; SAUḤ, PHAṬ to the weapon.
Thus, having simultaneously placed the six-limbed mantras on both hands in sequence from the thumbs to the palms,

and having again performed the triple-clapping and the binding of the directions with the *astra* mantra, one should perform the placement [of the mantras] upon the heart and the other five limbs using their respective mudrās; this is the ritual placement of the six limbs (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*).
15b) Now, the ritual placement for purifying the hands (karaśuddhinyāsa): therein, on the two middle fingers, *oṃ aṃ namaḥ*.
On the two ring fingers: Oṃ Ā Namaḥ. On the two little fingers: Oṃ Sauḥ Namaḥ.
To the index fingers: Oṃ AṂ Namaḥ. To the thumbs: Ā Namaḥ.
Oṃ sauḥ namaḥ to the two palms of the hands.
Then, one should perform the mutual wiping of the hands with all [the fingers]; this is the Karaśuddhi-nyāsa (the ritual placement for the purification of the hands).
16a) Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the four seats.
At the two feet: Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, salutation to the seat of the Goddess's own self.
HAIṂ HKLĪṂ HSAUṂ, [salutation] twice to the seat of all cakras.
At the two knees: hsai& hsklī& hskau& for the seat of all mantras, [twice].
At the *mūlādhāra*: Oṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Vlaṃ, twice for the *sādhyāsiddhāsana*.
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the four seats.
Then, furthermore, the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa) should be performed.
Then, the depositing [of the mantras] for the merchant woman and so forth.
Oṃ a& 16 vlū&; obeisance to Vaśinī, the goddess of speech. [On the head.]
Kaṃ 5 Klphrīṃ, [salutation] to Kāmeśvarī Vāgdevatā twice; [this is for] the forehead.
Caṃ 5 Nvlīṃ, twice to Mohanī Vāgdevatā; Bhrūṃ in the middle of the eyebrows.
Ṭa& 5 Glū& to the stainless goddess of speech (Vimalāvāgdevatā) twice.
17a) In the throat.
Taṃ 5 hrīṃ, to the goddess Aruṇāvāgdevatā, twice, in the heart.
Paṃ 5 Hslvryūṃ, [offering] to Jayanī Vāgdevatā at the navel.
Yaṃ 4 smyūṃ, to the Mistress of All, the Goddess of Speech, at the Mūlādhāra.
ŚAṂ 5 KṢSRĪṂ, to the goddess of speech Kaulinī, twice; from the *mūlādhāra* to the two ankles.
Thus ends the placement of Vaśinī.

Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with the root mantra preceded and followed by the *praṇava* (Oṃ), and having likewise performed three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should perform the placement of the root mantra upon the nine mudrās beginning with Saṃkṣobhinī.
17b) Then follows the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhā-nyāsa). Next is the placement of the nine wombs (navayoni-nyāsa).
Oṃ ai& hrī& śrī& ai& namaḥ to the right ear.
4 KRĪM, salutation to the left ear; 4 SAUḤ, salutation to the chin.
18a) 4 Aiṃ Namaḥ on the right cheek; 4 Klīṃ Namaḥ on the left cheek.
4 Sauḥ, salutation to the mouth; 4 Aiṃ, salutation to the right eye.
4 klīṃ, salutation to the left eye; 4 sauḥ, salutation to the nostril.
4 Aiṃ, obeisance to the right arm. 4 Klīṃ, obeisance to the left arm.
4 Sauḥ, obeisance to the heart. 4 Aiṃ, obeisance to the right elbow.
4 klīṃ, salutation to the left elbow.
18b) 4 *sauḥ* namaḥ to the belly; 4 *aiṃ* namaḥ to the right knee.
4 klīṃ, obeisance to the left knee; 4 sauḥ, obeisance to the *liṅga*.
4 aiṃ namaḥ to the right foot. 4 klīṃ namaḥ to the left foot.
Sauḥ, salutation to the base of the liṅga. Ai& (Aiṃ), salutation to the right side of the belly.
4 klīṃ, salutation to the left side of the abdomen; 4 sauḥ, salutation to the stomach.
4. Ai, salutation to the right breast.
19a) 4 klīṃ, salutation to the left breast; 4 sauḥ, salutation to the throat.
Thus ends the Nyāsa of the Nine Yonis. Now follows the Śrīcakra Nyāsa.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the Bindu-cakra.
In the aperture of Brahmā (the *brahmarandhra*).
Salutation to the triangle wheel (trikoṇacakra); [place this] on the forehead.
Salutation to the eight-spoked wheel. [This is for] the two eyebrows.
Salutation to the Antardaśāracakra; [place it] on the throat.
19b) Homage to the outer ten-spoked wheel in the heart.
4. Homage to the fourteen-spoked wheel at the navel.
4. Homage to the eight-petaled lotus at the *liṅga*.
4. Salutation to the sixteen-petaled lotus at the throat.
Salutation to the square wheel for the feet.
Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) within the Śrīcakra.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the four seats (catuṣpīṭha).
Aiṃ Kaṃ 5, in the fire-wheel (agnicakra) at the sacred seat (pīṭha) of Kāmagiri, O Goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī, whose essence is the Lord Maitrīśānanda,
the glorious power (śakti) of the Self of Śrī Rudra, obeisance to the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā) at the root-support (mūlādhāra).

20a) *Klīṃ Haṃ*. To the venerable Goddess Vajreśvarī, who is the essence of the Lord of the Sixth (*Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha*) in the solar wheel (*sūryacakra*) at the sacred seat (*pīṭha*) of Jālandhara; to the venerable Power whose self is the universe (*viśvātmaśakti*); salutation to the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*). [Salutation to] the heart.

Sauḥ Saṃ 4. To the venerable goddess Bhagamālinī, who is of the nature of Uḍḍīśanātha at the seat of Pūrṇagiri in the Moon-circle (somacakra), the venerable power of the self of Brahmā; salutation to her venerable sandals on the forehead.
20b) Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Kaṃ 15. To the venerable Śrī Caryānandanātha, the essence of the Vrahmacakra at the Oḍiyāna pīṭha;
to the goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the supreme Brahman-ātma-śakti; salutation to the Śrī-pādukā in the aperture of Brahmā (vrahmarandhra).
21a) Thus ends the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the four seats (catuḥpīṭha). Next is the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Oṃ ai& hrī& śrī& ai& ka& 5, salutation to the Heart, O Omniscient One, O Power, O Abode of all powers!
4 klīṃ haṃ 6, to Nityatṛptā (the Ever-Satisfied One) and Nityatṛptidhāman (the Abode of Eternal Contentment), svāhā to the head!
4 *sauḥ* *saṃ* 4. To the primordial awakener (*anādivodhinī*), to the abode of primordial awakening (*anādivodhidhāman*), to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*.
4 Sauḥ Saṃ 4, for the sake of Sovereignty, in the abode of the Power of Sovereignty, Hūṃ to the armor!
4 klīṃ haṃ 6, to the one whose power is eternally dissolved, to the abode of eternal dissolution, to that which is situated therein—vauṣaṭ!
4 Aiṃ Kaṃ 5 To Anantāyai, to Anantāyai, to the abode of infinite power, to the Weapon [mantra], Phaṭ!
Thus ends the six-limbed ritual placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Having performed the pervasive sprinkling with the root mantra, one should likewise perform the three-fold regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma).
22a) The placement of the root mantra is performed by binding the nine mudrās, beginning with Saṃkṣobhiṇī.
Then one should meditate.
I worship the Supreme Goddess, who has the luster of the orb of the rising sun, who possesses four arms and three eyes, and who holds a noose, a goad, arrows, and a bow.
Having thus meditated on [the deity] as one with oneself, one should place a flower upon one's own head.
Having meditated once again upon [the deity] within the lotus of the heart.
Having honored Mānasa, one should worship.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Laṃ; I offer fragrance, whose essence is earth; obeisance.
[To the two little fingers.]
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ, I offer this flower whose nature is space; homage!
[To] the two index fingers.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Raṃ, I offer this lamp consisting of radiant energy; homage!
[To the two middle fingers].
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vaṃ; I offer this water-natured food oblation; salutations.
23a) [The mudrā] of the ring finger.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ! I offer this betel leaf, whose nature is emptiness; homage!
By means of the yoni-mudrā.

Having recited the root-vidyā according to one's capacity, and having offered oblations, praised, and bowed, and having obtained permission from her, one should perform the worship with clarified butter.
Alternatively, as for the worship of the statement: having drawn the Śrīcakra there, one should place a flower in the center with the root mantra in reverse order and set it before [the deity].
23b) Then follows the placement of the conch shell.
One should draw a triangle, a circle, and a square.
Oṃ, homage to the all-pervading maṇḍala. [On] the seat.
Raṃ, salutation to the fire-maṇḍala; and Maṃ.
Haṃ, salutation to the solar disc. [The conch.]
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Laṃ Kha Na Thaṃ Ne.
Saṃ, salutation to the lunar disc.
The Six-Limbed Worship of Vālāṣa.
24a) hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ pādukāṃ ||
Perform the invocation and other rites; then display the dhenumudrā.
One should recite it seven times with the root mantra.
Sprinkling with the Gāyatrī mantra.
Aiṃ! O Goddess Tripurā, we know you; Klīṃ! O Kāmeśvarī, may we meditate upon you; Sauḥ! O you whose body is moist with nectar, impel us.
